sense: go through, find out by trying

terms.gloss: try; in the perfect, know from experience
evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.9.3: illud tibi expertus prōmittō et spondeō
Cic. Planc. 22: dīcō expertus in nōbīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: expertus, “from my own experience”; expertus sum, “I have been through it”. “An experience” has no single Latin noun: quod expertus sum, what I went through.

phrases.latin: illud tibi expertus prōmittō et spondeō
phrases.english: this I promise and guarantee you from my own experience

phrases.latin: Sed et illud, quod vel Polliōnis vel tamquam Polliōnis accēpī, vērissimum experior
phrases.english: and I find by experience that the saying I was given as Pollio’s, or as good as his, is very true

sources: Cicero’s and Pliny’s letters checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
